paragraphs: Abba bar Marta, who is Abba bar Minyomi. Gittin 37b; Yevamot 120a: the exilarch’s household had a monetary claim against him. He brought wax and stuck a worn cloth to his forehead, passed before them, and they did not recognize him. Gittin 37b: he paid Rabbah during the Sabbatical year. For this the exilarch released him from the money he owed him, because he was a Torah scholar. At the end of chapter Kol Kitvei, 121, end of b: the exilarch’s household had a monetary claim and was troubling him. Spittle lay there on Shabbat; a vessel was brought and overturned over it. He told them, “You need not,” etc. He said, “He is a Torah scholar; leave him.” In Mo'ed Katan 26, end of b, he went to comfort Rava in mourning, and Rava said of him, “How little understanding this Torah scholar has!” Yoma 84a: a rabid dog bit him and his mother made him a gold tube. He asked Abaye, Beitzah 22a. Minyomi, Rav Nachman’s colleague, was in Rabbah’s time. Rabbi Abbahu, Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha, Abba bar Minyomi, Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa, and Rav Safra: Rava said, “Rav Safra has worsted three ordained rabbis.” Rav Ashi said, “How has he worsted them?”, Gittin 29b. This requires examination: Rav Ashi was born when Rava died. Perhaps Rav Ashi spoke about the matter Rava had stated earlier, but Rashi’s wording, “Rav Ashi said to him,” implies he spoke to Rava. Perhaps Rashi has a scribal error and should read “Rav Ashi said.” (Perhaps he lived long, being in Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha’s time, in the generation of Rabbi Yochanan and Resh Lakish, and also in Abaye and Rava’s time.)
